segments: The seventh {OCR?} generation of the Roman kings.
[Valentinian]
And he was strong and wise.
And he brought his brother Valens and made him king in the East.
And when he went to Rome, he proclaimed his son Gratian as Augustus,
and made him consul.
And in his eleventh year,
Ardashir, the son of Shapur, reigned over the Persians for four years.
And at this time Procopius rebelled against Valens.
And when he was captured in Constantinople, he was tied to two trees and torn asunder.
Now Valens, while he was on his way to Egypt and arrived at Marcianopolis,
a great earthquake occurred, and the sea was stirred up,
and it threw small boats over the walls of the city.
And the sea retreated from its place,
and large ships remained as if on dry land.
And the people of the city ran to plunder,
and the sea returned upon them and covered them,
and they were drowned.
Now Valentinian, while his wife was still alive,
took another wife, radiant in beauty,
and he abolished the law,
and permitted that anyone who wished
might possess two [wives] together.
And when he went to war against the Sarmatians,
they were afraid and sent envoys for peace.
And when he saw that they were contemptible {OCR?} [people], he cried out loudly:
"How evilly situated is the Roman Empire,
that a people as contemptible {OCR?} and feeble as this should dare to make war!"
And in that very outcry, the veins of his neck ruptured,
and much blood flowed from him, and he died.
And because Gratian, his firstborn son, was not near,
the troops assembled and made king his younger son, whom he had by Justina, his last wife, whom he had married on account of her beauty,
who was also called by the name of his father.
Valens, moreover, made Gratian a general and sent him to the war with the Goths,
and he did not succeed.
And to Valens himself an oracle came forth,
that he whose name began with the letter Tau
would reign after him.
He commanded that everyone who was called Theodore,
and Theodotus,
and the like of these,
should be put to death.
And at this time there were seen in the air men amid the clouds in the form of armed men.
And there was born in Antioch an infant who had one eye in the middle of the sockets of the eyes,
and four hands,
and four legs,
and a beard.
And at this time the Arabs were stirred up against the land of the Romans,
and there was reigning over them a woman whose name was Mawiyya.
Then they made peace...
